turns.content: I brought a glimble to show you.
I do not know what you mean by glimble. What is it in your game?
It is my name for a knitted toy whale.
Then your glimble is the knitted toy whale. What color did you make it?
My made-up word is plimsy.
What does plimsy mean in your story?
It means pleasantly sleepy after a long walk.
That sounds cozy. Your character feels plimsy after the walk.
Do you know what my grandfather calls a skiddle?
I do not know his meaning. Can you tell me?
It is his nickname for the little kitchen stool.
Now I understand. When he says skiddle, he means the little stool.
I made a badge with the word moonbutton on it.
Moonbutton is a fun word. Did you invent a meaning for it?
Yes. It means a shiny round stone in our club.
Then the badge can show a shiny round stone so your club remembers.
I want that one.
Which one do you mean? Tell me its color or where it is.
The tiny red bowl on the left.
You mean the tiny red bowl on the left.
Can you help me fix it?
Tell me what needs fixing.
The wing on my paper bird is folded down.
Try gently unfolding that paper wing. Keep the bird dry while you work.
That answer was not about my question.
I missed your point. Please tell me which part you wanted answered.
I asked where the toy is, not what it looks like.
You are asking for its location. Where did you last see the toy?
I have a surprise, but I have not told you what it is.
Then I do not know the surprise yet. Will you tell me?
I learned to skip with a rope.
That is exciting! How long can you keep skipping now?
The small balloon is pink. The large balloon is black.
The small one is pink, and the large one is black.
Sorry, I meant the large balloon is white.
Thanks for the correction. The large balloon is white; the small one is still pink.
I thought my model boat was made of wood, but it is made of cork.
Your model boat is made of cork.
What material should I write on its card?
Write cork on the card.
I said the basket was outside. I was mistaken; it is inside the porch.
The basket is inside the porch.
Should I search the garden for it?
No. You corrected the location to inside the porch.
I used to call my toy rabbit Hoppy. Now I call it Pip.
Your toy rabbit's current name is Pip.
Which name should we use now?
Pip, the new name you chose.
My drawing shows a crab conducting an orchestra with a carrot.
That is a funny baton for a pretend conductor! The carrot could point to each musician.
Does the carrot really make music?
No. The musicians make the music; the carrot is the crab's pretend baton.
My toy frog owns a bakery that sells pebble cupcakes.
A pebble bakery works nicely in a pretend game. You could arrange the pebbles on a toy tray.
Can I eat a pebble cupcake?
No. Real pebbles are not food. They can only be pretend cupcakes.
I drew an octopus knitting eight scarves at once.
Eight scarves would make a wonderfully busy picture.
Are real octopuses taught to knit scarves?
No. The knitting is a funny imaginary activity in your drawing.
I made a tiny paper umbrella for your picture.
A paper umbrella will look sweet above the fish in the picture.
Should I drop the paper into your water?
No. Keep it on the picture, outside my tank.
My cardboard castle has four towers, but only one has a flag.
One of the four towers has a flag.
How many towers have no flag?
Three towers have no flag.
The red wagon belongs to me. The yellow wagon belongs to my sister.
Your wagon is red, and your sister's is yellow.
Which wagon belongs to my sister?
The yellow wagon belongs to your sister.
I set a striped marble next to a spotted marble.
There are two marbles beside each other: one striped and one spotted.
Which marble has dots on it?
The spotted marble has dots.
I saved a seat for my friend beside the door.
Your friend's seat is beside the door.
Is that the seat by the window?
No. You said beside the door, not by the window.
My friend has different beliefs from my family, and we both like making puppets.
You can enjoy making puppets together while respecting your different beliefs.
Do our puppets have to tell the same stories?
No. Each of you can tell a story that matters to you.
My cousin is quiet while our family prays.
Your cousin may prefer to listen quietly.
Should I make him say the words?
No. You can let him choose whether to join in.
Whilst I arrange these flowers, can you count the three white ones?
There are three white flowers.
I added one more white flower. How many now?
Now there are four white flowers.
Methinks my pretend pirate needs a smaller hat. This one covers his eyes.
A smaller hat would let him see in your story.
Could I just move this hat higher instead?
Yes. Moving it higher could leave his eyes uncovered too.
